path.name: Software Systems with AI Agents
path.description: A live program where builders use Claude Code, Codex, and other AI agents to design real software systems, then prove the work by building a simulated population to test it against — the same persona-and-verifier pattern behind population-scale AI research like MatrAIx — before shipping it live.
path.targetAudience: First- and second-year CS and CS-adjacent students who want hands-on experience with AI coding agents before their coursework gets there, also open to coding bootcamp participants, self-taught builders, and career switchers who want to become software system architects. No formal enrollment required, just comfort writing and reading code.

programs.name: How to Create Software Systems with AI Agents
programs.description: A two-week live cohort built for first- and second-year CS (and CS-adjacent) students, Monday through Thursday, where builders use Claude Code, Codex, and other AI agents to design real software systems: databases, APIs, and architecture. In the second week you reverse-engineer the persona-and-simulation architecture behind population-scale AI research like MatrAIx, build a small simulated population, and ship a system tested against it live, mapped to one of AutoNateAI's real banking consulting offerings.
programs.learningOutcomes: Set up and direct AI coding agents responsibly, engineer prompts and context for real projects, design relational and graph data models, build and query APIs, document architecture with Mermaid diagrams, review and debug AI-generated code, design a simulated population using the persona-and-verifier pattern reverse-engineered from population-scale AI research, and ship a working system tested against that simulation.
programs.projectSummary: A real software system paired with the simulated population that tests it: a persona cohort and scenario set built the same way population-scale AI research like MatrAIx builds theirs, mapped to one of AutoNateAI's banking consulting offerings, plus a working data model, API, and application, built with AI agents and documented like production work.
programs.portfolioArtifact: Your Git repository with the shipped system, commits, architecture notes and Mermaid diagrams, your persona and scenario spec, the simulation findings, and a final reflection on what the agents got right, what they got wrong, and what you fixed.
programs.cohortNote: Next cohort: Monday, August 17, 2026, two weeks, Monday-Thursday, 6:00-7:30 PM CST. The same rhythm continues afterward as Saturday Live Builds, open to everyone.

sessions.name: Session 1: Meet Your AI Agents
sessions.objectives: Set up Claude Code and Codex as real collaborators and learn to point an agent at an unfamiliar codebase before asking it to change anything.
sessions.liveActivity: Install and configure Claude Code and Codex, walk through a real repository together, and have an agent explain its architecture, entry points, and data flow back to you.
sessions.homework: Use an agent to map a small existing codebase and write a short architecture note describing its components and how they connect.

sessions.name: Session 2: Prompt and Context Engineering in Practice
sessions.objectives: Apply prompt and context engineering to a real multi-file project: structure the ask, and give the agent only the context it actually needs.
sessions.liveActivity: Take a real feature request, structure a prompt with role, task, and constraints, hand the agent the relevant files, and review the diff line by line.
sessions.homework: Use an agent to implement one small feature in an existing project and document what context you gave it, what you accepted, and what you rejected.

sessions.name: Session 3: Databases and APIs
sessions.objectives: Design a relational schema for a real problem, wire up a simple API, and use an agent to scaffold both responsibly.
sessions.liveActivity: Design tables, keys, and relationships for a sample system, build API endpoints against them, and query the data live.
sessions.homework: Add one table and one API endpoint to a project, and write the query that answers a real question about the data.

sessions.name: Session 4: System Architecture and Mermaid Diagrams
sessions.objectives: Turn a working system into a diagram: use Mermaid to communicate architecture and organize services and components.
sessions.liveActivity: Pick a real system, diagram it in Mermaid, identify its weak points, and talk through tradeoffs with an agent.
sessions.homework: Produce a Mermaid architecture diagram for your own project and one paragraph explaining a tradeoff you made.

sessions.name: Session 5: Debugging and Reviewing AI-Generated Code
sessions.objectives: Build the habit of reviewing agent output like a senior engineer: reading diffs, running tests, and catching hallucinated logic.
sessions.liveActivity: Review a batch of AI-generated changes live, find at least one real bug or hallucination, fix it, and commit the working version.
sessions.homework: Review and correct one AI-generated change in your own project, documenting what was wrong and why.

sessions.name: Session 6: Designing Your Simulated Population
sessions.objectives: Reverse-engineer the persona-and-verifier pattern behind population-scale AI simulation research like MatrAIx, and use it to define a small synthetic population for a real AutoNateAI banking offering.
sessions.liveActivity: Pick one AutoNateAI banking consulting offering, define a cohort of persona agents for it (borrowers, loan officers, or customers), and draft the scenarios and verifiers they'll run through.
sessions.homework: Write the persona schema and scenario spec for your simulated population: who they are, what they're trying to do, and how you'll know if the system handled it well.

sessions.name: Session 7: Build Week Part 1 - Design and Start the System
sessions.objectives: Turn the persona cohort and scenario spec into a real system design, and start building both the software and the simulated agents that will test it, live.
sessions.liveActivity: Design the architecture for the chosen system, scaffold the repository, wire up the first persona agent, and implement the first real feature with agent support.
sessions.homework: Keep building: commit progress, expand the simulated population, and update the architecture notes as the design changes.

sessions.name: Session 8: Build Week Part 2 - Ship It
sessions.objectives: Finish a working version of the system, run your simulated population through it, and capture what the findings say about whether the design holds up.
sessions.liveActivity: Finish the build, run the full persona cohort through it live, demo the findings, and write up what the simulation exposed.
sessions.homework: Submit final repo link, architecture notes, your persona and scenario spec, the simulation findings, and a short system writeup.
